protections: P1: a client-supplied temp-file name in the zipdl download step must stay inside the volume temp dir (elFinder.class.php:1625-1629)
P2: a path decoded from a client hash must resolve inside the volume root before it is used (_stat in-root check, elFinderVolumeLocalFileSystem.class.php:457-460, via _inpath/getFullPath)

P3: a client-supplied file/dir name joined onto a target dir must not contain path separators or parent segments (nameAccepted, elFinderVolumeDriver.class.php:3574-3588; _joinPath, elFinderVolumeLocalFileSystem.class.php:290-292)

evidence: php/elFinder.class.php:1625 $file = $targets[1] taken straight from the request
php/elFinder.class.php:1626 joined onto getTempPath() with no basename or separator check
php/elFinder.class.php:1628 the path is registered in elFinderTempFiles, and onShutdown unlinks it (php/elFinder.class.php:4393-4396), so the route can both read and delete
php/elFinder.class.php:1649 fopen on the joined path; the contents are streamed back as the download
php/elFinder.class.php:1610 step 1 only ever hands out basename($path), so a bare filename is the only legitimate value

traps.reason_to_dismiss: a fix that rejects '/' looks complete on a POSIX host; the backslash only acts as a separator on Windows
evidence: php/elFinder.class.php:1626 joins with DIRECTORY_SEPARATOR and does nothing to '\\' in $file, so a check for '/' alone misses the Windows separator

traps.reason_to_dismiss: _stat already runs an in-root check with the comment 'Prevents directory traveral' and hashes are opaque, so decode looks guarded
evidence: php/elFinderVolumeLocalFileSystem.class.php:393 _abspath joins the decoded relative path onto root with no normalisation, so the relative path '..' becomes '<root>/..'
php/elFinderVolumeLocalFileSystem.class.php:389-391 a decoded path that starts with the separator is returned unchanged ('for link')
php/elFinderVolumeDriver.class.php:6120 the normalising regex only collapses 'seg/../' when a separator follows, so a trailing '/..' survives
php/elFinderVolumeLocalFileSystem.class.php:422 _inpath then does a lexical prefix test; '<root>/..' starts with '<root>/' and passes
php/elFinderVolumeLocalFileSystem.class.php:458 _stat accepts the parent of root as an in-volume directory
php/elFinderVolumeDriver.class.php:2038-2055 mkdir/upload (2217-2285) then _joinPath under that dir writes into the parent of root

traps.reason_to_dismiss: every create/rename already calls nameAccepted, and the default acceptedName regex looks like a deliberate name policy, not a path check
evidence: php/elFinderVolumeDriver.class.php:383 the default acceptedName '/^[^\.].*/' only rejects a leading dot; 'sub/../../x' passes
php/elFinderVolumeDriver.class.php:2034, 2078, 2137 mkdir, mkfile and rename gate on nameAccepted only
php/elFinderVolumeDriver.class.php:2049, 2150 the isNameExists probe goes through _stat, returns empty for the out-of-root path, and so does not block
php/elFinderVolumeDriver.class.php:3956 allowCreate is an attribute check only, with no containment
php/elFinderVolumeLocalFileSystem.class.php:291 _joinPath concatenates the name verbatim; _mkdir:795, _mkfile:814 and _move:868 act on the result
php/elFinderVolumeDropbox2.class.php:73, php/elFinderVolumeFTP.class.php:145, php/elFinderVolumeBox.class.php:105 the other drivers set an acceptedName that forbids '/', but LocalFileSystem does not

traps.reason_to_dismiss: PHP strips directories from $_FILES names, so uploads look safe; the override only fires for clipboard 'image*' uploads
evidence: php/elFinder.class.php:2915-2917 when the uploaded name starts with 'image', it is replaced by the raw request value $args['name'][$i]
php/elFinderVolumeDriver.class.php:2225 upload validates it only with nameAccepted (same default regex as T4)
php/elFinderVolumeLocalFileSystem.class.php:909 _save joins the name verbatim and writes the uploaded content there

masking: T3 masks a second weakness: once '<root>/..' passes _stat, _scandir (php/elFinderVolumeLocalFileSystem.class.php:676-752) caches stats for every child of the parent dir without an _inpath check, so a listing outside root becomes visible within the request. A T3 fix closes it too, so it is not counted separately.
T2 can only be reached or observed on a Windows host; under a POSIX test runner it stays latent behind T1.

conflicts.what: hardening _inpath with realpath() would reject in-root symlinks whose targets lie outside root, which followSymLinks deliberately supports (php/elFinderVolumeLocalFileSystem.class.php:465-483, php/elFinderVolumeLocalFileSystem.class.php:389-391 'for link'); the fix has to normalise lexically, or treat only the trailing '..' as the bad case

folder upload sends 'a/b/c' paths in dirs[], and this must keep working; it is split on '/' before volume->mkdir (php/elFinder.class.php:1853), so rejecting separators in nameAccepted is safe, but a fix in core elFinder::mkdir/rename alone would leave T5 open

fairness_risks: Names that contain '..' but no separator (e.g. 'a..b.txt') are legitimate and must stay accepted; a rule like 'reject any ..' over-refuses.

On POSIX a backslash is a legal filename character; refusing '\\' in every name to cover T2 would break legitimate Linux filenames. T2 should be tested only on the zipdl temp-name parameter, never on user file names.
Symlinks inside root that point outside root are supported when followSymLinks is on (php/elFinderVolumeLocalFileSystem.class.php:465-483); tests must not require realpath containment for them.
The zipdl step-2 value is always a bare basename handed out by step 1 (php/elFinder.class.php:1610); that round trip must keep working.

design.why: These are three independent guard sites in different files with different reasons to dismiss. T1 is the advisory surface the report points at (zipdl temp name, absent check). T3 is a how-type lexical-normalisation flaw hidden behind an existing, commented in-root check; it is the mimo-type trap and has a coupled must-keep value (symlink following). T4 is an absent separator check behind a validator that is already called; it is the deepseek-type trap. T5 can be added as an M1 route of T4's guard to penalise fixes made only at command level, but it does not add an independent group. T2 is left out because it is Windows-only and untestable on a POSIX grader.
